applies_why: The text decides whether Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 count as unanswered witnesses against link C3, which is exactly what the rule governs.
quote: the line is cured by retraction, not defended: every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link and a listed premise and names that round
room: The BROKEN line quoted in the text rests on a witness-left-unanswered ground, which could be read as a count made without the required quotation. The text retracts that ground, so I read the retraction as controlling and not as a count.
why: The text withdraws the witness-left-unanswered ground and regrades the collision UNDERDETERMINED, so it counts no verse as an unanswered witness and does not breach K-G4.
